Natasha Howard has cleared 7+ points in 93% of her 44 games this season, and is riding a 16-game streak of doing it. She's hitting 100% over her last 10 and 100% over her last 5, averaging 14.4 points on the season (14.4 across her last 5) — the 7+ line sits well below her normal output. Priced -650 at Fanatics.

Kiki Iriafen has cleared 7+ rebounds in 78% of her 41 games this season, and is riding a 13-game streak of doing it. She's hitting 100% over her last 10 and 100% over her last 5, averaging 9.4 rebounds on the season (11.4 across her last 5) — the 7+ line sits well below her normal output. Priced -630 at Fanatics.

Two legs from two different games at a combined -297 — each leg stands on its own record, and neither result can drag the other down.
propPlay.analysis: {"analysis":"Natasha Howard carries a 16-game clearing streak on the 7+ points line, hitting it in 93% of her 44 games this season with a season average of 14.4 points, giving her a +7.4 cushion above the line. That kind of depth below her mean is what makes this an alternate line worth taking: she is not being asked to hit her ceiling, just her floor. On the other side, Kiki Iriafen has cleared 7+ rebounds in 13 straight games, with a 78% season hit rate across 41 games and a season average of 9.4, though that average jumps to 11.4 over her last 5 games, creating a +2.4 cushion that is thinner but still meaningful. The parlay structure isolates the risk: Indiana Fever at Minnesota Lynx is one universe of variables, Connecticut Sun at Washington Mystics is entirely separate, so a blowout or foul trouble in one game does not automatically wreck the other. To cash this ticket, both players must clear their respective lines in their own games on the same day. The real leverage here is Howard's consistency and the depth of her floor, but the parlay lives or dies on executing both legs, and Iriafen's thinner cushion against her 7+ rebounds line is where the second leg carries its weight.","quickTake":["Natasha Howard has cleared 7+ in 16 straight games with a season average of 14.4 points, placing her 7.4 points above the line and establishing a floor-level ask rather than a ceiling play.","Kiki Iriafen's 13-game clearing streak and 100% hit rate over her last 10 games anchor the second leg, even though her +2.4 season-average cushion is narrower than Howard's.","The two-game structure means each leg stands independent; a blowout or foul situation in Minnesota does not force a loss if Washington delivers.","Combined hit rates of 93% and 78% season-to-date, both at 100% over the last 10 and last 5 games, produce a parlay with concrete recent form behind both components."],"devilsAdvocate":["Iriafen's +2.4 cushion is thin enough that a single quiet night on the boards, or early foul trouble forcing reduced minutes, can easily push her below 7 rebounds even while her season trajectory points upward.","Both legs must land on the same day; if Natasha Howard clears 7+ but Iriafen falls short at 6 rebounds, the parlay loses regardless of Howard's consistency, and a two-player parlay failure rate of roughly 5-6% is real money when the legs are this close to execution."]}
